entities.summary: He Xiu was a Chinese philosopher and philologist during the Later Han dynasty. He was a prominent representative of the New Text school. He rose to become the chief advisor to the emperor. He is the author of commentaries on the Gongyang Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals, titled Chunqiu Gongyang jiegu 春秋公羊解詁, which was part of the History of the Later Han. Many of his works are lost or only preserved in fragments. He was influenced by Dong Zhongshu. His Theory of the Three Ages had a decisive influence on the development of Kang Youwei’s (1858–1927) utopian theory.
